_comment: What a clean install from the internet actually contains, measured rather than assumed.
This file exists so that a missing texture is not mistaken for a broken install. Somebody
setting SCOPE up for the first time, human or agent, opens a scene, sees that 46 images
cannot be found, and reasonably concludes the download failed. It did not. Those files were
never published, because they were never recoverable: the scene authors used relative paths
pointing outside the scene folder, and in two cases an absolute path into a paid Blender
So the state below is the expected state. scripts/06_verify_setup.py checks against it and
reports three different things rather than one:
matches expected  the install is correct, even where files are absent
worse             more is missing than should be, so the download or unpack failed
better            fewer are missing, which means someone has fixed a scene and this file
None of this affects a benchmark run. SCOPE captures the viewport with studio lighting,
which does not draw the scene world, so a missing sky never reaches the model. The missing
surface textures in postwar-city show as one magenta door and a few flat panels in a scene
Measured on a clean clone of main plus scripts/03_download_scenes.sh, Blender 4.4.3.

book-nook.note: Complete. The only scene with a working sky, packed into the .blend.

city-street.note: Complete. It has no world environment texture at all, which is how it was authored rather than something absent.

postwar-city.note: 46 surface textures are absent and not recoverable from any published source. They live under texture/batiment, texture/ciment, texture/route, texture/barriere, texture/plantes and world/masks, by relative paths pointing outside the scene folder. The scene renders usably without them: one magenta door and a few flat panels.

whitechapel.note: Five absent. Two are HDRIs from a paid Blender addon on the original author's Windows machine, one is from free-hdri-skies.com which no longer exists, two are scene-author textures. The sky has never worked in this scene; it is the original state rather than a regression. Studio lighting means it is never drawn, so no capture is affected.
